messages:
maria: :rotating_light: Heads up — I'm seeing a spike in OTEL tracing errors and lots of orphaned spans after last night's LB failover in us-west2. Grafana trace waterfall shows multiple root spans for the same request id, parent-child relationships broken. Anyone digging?
aj: I saw the Prom alert fire `otel_instrumentation_errors` around 02:13. SLO dashboard shows tail latency bump. Quick look at ingress logs suggests `traceparent` gets dropped on some requests that hit the new GCLB backends — looks like header rewrite.
sam: Which LB and region? can you share the grafana panel? https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/trace/ingress?panelId=7
maria: GCLB -> us-west2. This started immediately after the failover caused by a BGP flap. I pulled a sample trace id 0af7651916cd43b1a0f0b1c9e0 — ingress has a root span, then service-front shows a new root span instead of a child.
irene: Can you paste the envoy/ingress logs around that trace id? Also, does our otel-collector have `replace_remote_parent` enabled? We recently rolled a config change.
maria: here's the relevant collector snippet I found in prod config (from k8s configmap):
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      http: {}
processors:
  batch: {}
  memory_limiter: {}
exporters:
  otlphttp:
    endpoint: "http://collector-remote:4318"
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [memory_limiter, batch]
      exporters: [otlphttp]
  telemetry:
    logs: true
# NOTE: a recent prod rollout included: replace_remote_parent: true in the attributes processor (looks suspicious)
```
deploy-bot: deploy-ops: rolled otel-collector v1.21 -> prod at 01:50 with config change `replace_remote_parent: true` (release id: rs-2026-03-18-otlp).
aj: bingo. `replace_remote_parent: true` will drop upstream trace parents and generate new ones. We should accept upstream ids since GCLB is upstream. Set it to `false`. Also ensure the LB is not stripping `traceparent`/`b3` headers.
sam: I can roll a revert to set `replace_remote_parent: false` and restart collector pods. @irene do you want me to do the rollback now?
irene: yes please. Also, add a small validation: after rollback, run a curl through the LB to ensure `traceparent` is preserved and verify the trace shows single root -> child spans. Add a promrule: alert if `traceparent_missing_rate > 0.5%` sustained 5m.
nina: fyi some runtimes re-create ids when headers exceed size limits — we saw header bloat from baggage + cookies in some requests during the flap. If the LB truncated headers we could also see regenerated spans. We should cap baggage size and strip big cookies at the proxy.
maria: good point. I also found env logs showing `header_too_large` warnings at the LB for a small subset. I'll open a follow-up to reduce baggage and add a test for header size.
sam: rolled the patch at 02:45, setting `replace_remote_parent: false`. Collector pods recycled, traces reconnected. Initial check: trace waterfalls look normal again, parent relationships preserved. Prom alert silenced.
maria: verified a bunch of traces, looks good. We'll still add the runbook: preflight check for header passthrough on LB failover and ensure collector config maintains upstream trace ids.
ops-bot: Created IFR-783: "Ensure OTEL header passthrough on LB failover" assigned to eng-platform.
mar ia: thanks everyone — closing this thread once the runbook PR lands. :thumbsup:
